mainTopic: The supremacy of יראת שמים, verses about the wicked, רבי יוסי's view on extinguishing a flame, and the three מצוות tied to childbirth
overview: This amud opens by finishing a parable: Torah without יראת שמים is like a treasurer who has only the inner keys. רבי ינאי and רב יהודה add that fear of Heaven is the courtyard behind the gate and the very purpose of creation. In a story, רבי סימון and רבי אלעזר praise רבי יעקב בר אחא in two different ways. The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר was the one who chose the higher praise, 'fearer of sin.' רב עולא and his son רבא בר רב עולא then explain verses about the wicked: do not add to sins you have already done, and the wicked know their end but stay untroubled. The גמרא returns to the משנה about putting out a flame and asks whether רבי יוסי follows רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון. עולא and רבי יוחנן give two different answers. A new משנה then lists three מצוות whose neglect endangers women at childbirth: נדה, חלה and lighting the lamp. The גמרא begins explaining why, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The treasurer without the outer key
steps.stepSummary: Torah without יראת שמים is like a treasurer who has the inner keys but not the outer key. He cannot get in.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A person with Torah but no] fear of Heaven is like a treasurer who was given the keys to the inner doors but was not given the keys to the outer door. How will he get in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began on the previous amud. That statement compares a person who has Torah but lacks יראת שמים to a treasurer who has the wrong set of keys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah is the 'inner key' and יראת שמים is the 'outer key.' The outer door comes first, so without fear of Heaven a person never reaches the inner rooms, which are true Torah. The point is that fear of Heaven is the entrance to Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear of Heaven; awe of ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The beginning of the statement (by רבה בר רב הונא, about someone who has Torah but lacks fear of Heaven) is on the previous lines of the daf.

phrases.english: [lacking] fear of Heaven, is like a treasurer
phrases.notes: This picks up a sentence that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: to whom they gave the keys of the inner doors
phrases.notes: The inner keys stand for Torah.

phrases.english: but the keys of the outer door they did not give him
phrases.notes: The outer key stands for fear of Heaven.

phrases.english: With what will he enter?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; the point is he can't get in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יראת שמים is the gateway. Without it, Torah knowledge cannot be truly accessed.

steps.title: A gate with no courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי gives a similar parable: it is pitiful to build a gate for a courtyard you do not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי would announce: Woe to one who has no courtyard but makes a gate for the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי adds a second parable with the same message as the treasurer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'courtyard' is יראת שמים and the 'gate' is Torah, which leads into it. Building a gate with nothing behind it is pointless. Learning Torah without fear of Heaven is empty in the same way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai would proclaim:
Woe to one who has no courtyard
phrases.notes: The courtyard stands for fear of Heaven.

phrases.english: yet makes a gate for the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel parable that supports the same theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah without יראת שמים is like a gate with no courtyard behind it.

steps.title: The world was created for fear of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says ה׳ created the world only so that people would fear Him, and brings a פסוק from קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, created His world only so that people would fear Him, as it says: 'And God has made it so that they should fear before Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה raises יראת שמים even higher. He says it is the whole purpose of creation, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier parables showed that fear of Heaven is needed in order to reach Torah. רב יהודה goes further and calls it the reason the world exists. The verse 'והאלהים עשה שייראו מלפניו' is read as ה׳'s stated goal in making everything.

keyTerms.meaning: That they should fear before Him
As it is said (introduces a verse)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, did not create His world
except so that people would fear before Him,
as it is said: 'And God has made it so that they should fear before Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same theme to the level of the purpose of creation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The purpose of creation is that people fear ה׳.

steps.title: Two sages praise a passing scholar in different ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימון and רבי אלעזר want to stand up for רבי יעקב בר אחא. One praises him as a fearer of sin, and the other praises him as a man of Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימון and רבי אלעזר were sitting. רבי יעקב בר אחא passed by. One said to the other: Let us stand before him, because he is a man who fears sin. The other said: Let us stand before him, because he is a man of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. Both sages agree to stand up, but they give different reasons. This sets up the protest in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages honor the scholar. The question is which quality is the bigger praise: יראת חטא (fear of sin) or Torah learning. The story ties back to the main theme of this section.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us stand up before him
A man of Torah; a Torah scholar

steps.confusionAlert: The story does not tell us which sage said which line. The גמרא works this out in steps 6 through 8.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סִימוֹן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הֲווֹ יָתְבִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Simon and Rabbi Elazar were sitting.

phrases.aramaic: חָלֵיף וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Acha passed by.
One said to his colleague:

phrases.aramaic: נֵיקוּ מִקַּמֵּיהּ, דִּגְבַר דָּחֵיל חֶטְאִין הוּא.
phrases.english: Let us stand before him, for he is a man who fears sin.
The other said to him:

phrases.aramaic: נֵיקוּ מִקַּמֵּיהּ, דִּגְבַר בַּר אוֹרְיָין הוּא.
phrases.english: Let us stand before him, for he is a man of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סִימוֹן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates the same theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two sages give two different reasons for honoring the same scholar.

steps.title: Fear of sin is the greater praise
steps.stepSummary: The first sage objects: 'I called him a fearer of sin, and you call him only a Torah scholar?!'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I told you he is a man who fears sin, and you tell me he is a man of Torah?!
steps.whatsHappening: The first sage protests the second sage's praise. In his view, calling someone a Torah scholar is a lesser compliment than calling him a fearer of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protest only makes sense if fear of sin is the higher level. Switching to 'Torah scholar' is treated as a step down. This matches everything earlier here about the supremacy of יראת שמים.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא דִּגְבַר דָּחֵיל חֶטְאִין הוּא,
phrases.english: I tell you that he is a man who fears sin,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרַתְּ לִי אַתְּ בַּר אוֹרְיָין הוּא?!
phrases.english: and you tell me he is a man of Torah?!
phrases.notes: He's protesting: calling him just a man of Torah lowered the praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the second sage's praise
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fear of sin is the greater praise, so calling him only a Torah scholar diminishes him.

steps.title: Proving that רבי אלעזר praised fear of sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אלעזר was the one who said 'fearer of sin,' because elsewhere he teaches that ה׳ has nothing in His world except יראת שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that it was רבי אלעזר who said 'he is a man who fears sin.' For רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in His world except fear of Heaven alone, as it says: 'And now, Israel, what does ה׳ your God ask of you, except to fear...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify which sage in the story said 'fearer of sin.' It proposes רבי אלעזר and brings his own teaching as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere רבי אלעזר says that יראת שמים is the only thing ה׳ truly 'has' in His world. Someone with that view would naturally choose 'fearer of sin' as the highest praise. The first proof is the פסוק 'מה ה׳ אלהיך שואל מעמך כי אם ליראה.'

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rabbi Elazar who said
that he is a man who fears sin.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in His world
except fear of Heaven alone,
as it is said: 'And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God'

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: ask of you, except to fear, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the speaker in the story
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר was the one who praised 'fear of sin'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's teaching, quoted by רבי יוחנן, that ה׳ has only יראת שמים in His world

steps.title: A second verse: 'הן' means 'one'
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק from איוב is brought: 'הן יראת ה׳ היא חכמה.' In Greek, 'הן' means 'one,' so fear of Heaven is the 'one' thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'And He said to man: Behold (הן), the fear of ה׳ is wisdom...' For in Greek they call 'one' הן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי אלעזר's teaching with a second verse. It reads the word 'הן' through Greek, where הן means 'one.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is read as 'One: fear of ה׳ is wisdom.' This shows that fear of Heaven is the single thing that matters most. It backs up the word 'בלבד' (alone) in רבי אלעזר's statement.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And He said to man:'

phrases.aramaic: הֵן יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא חׇכְמָה וְגוֹ׳״ —
phrases.english: 'Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, etc.'
for in the Greek language
they call 'one' hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second verse to רבי אלעזר's teaching
steps.raayaObject: That יראת שמים is the one and only thing
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 28:28, with 'הן' read as Greek for 'one'

steps.title: Conclusion: it was רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that רבי אלעזר was the one who praised fear of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude [so].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts its proposal. The speaker who said 'fearer of sin' was רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבי אלעזר teaches elsewhere that יראת שמים is the one thing ה׳ has, he must be the sage who preferred that praise. It follows that רבי סימון was the one who said 'בר אוריין.'
steps.whatToRemember: In this section יראת שמים outranks Torah knowledge alone. It is the outer key, the courtyard, the purpose of creation, and the 'one' thing ה׳ has. This is why רבי אלעזר insisted on the praise 'fearer of sin.'

phrases.english: Conclude [so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the identification
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר was the one who praised רבי יעקב בר אחא as a fearer of sin.

steps.title: Does the verse allow a little wickedness?
steps.stepSummary: רב עולא asks about the verse 'Do not be overly wicked.' Does that mean it is fine to be a little wicked?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עולא expounded: What is the meaning of what is written: 'Do not be overly wicked...'? Only 'overly' one should not be wicked, but a little one may be wicked?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עולא opens a new topic by pointing out a problem in a פסוק. Read literally, the verse seems to permit a small amount of sin. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הרבה' (overly) seems to suggest that a little wickedness is acceptable. That cannot be correct. רב עולא presents this as a difficulty that needs a better reading of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. It is not part of the story about רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Ulla expounded:
What is meant by what is written: 'Do not be overly wicked, etc.'?
Is it only overly that one should not be wicked,
but a little one may be wicked?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'אל תרשע הרבה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'overly' implies that a little wickedness is permitted, which cannot be correct.

steps.title: The garlic parable
steps.stepSummary: רב עולא answers: someone who already ate garlic and smells should not eat more and smell worse. If you have sinned a little, do not add to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: One who ate garlic and his breath smells, should he go and eat more garlic so that his smell spreads even more?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עולא resolves the difficulty with a parable about garlic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is not permitting a little sin. It speaks to someone who has already sinned and warns him not to think, 'I'm already bad, so I may as well continue.' Just as eating more garlic only makes the smell worse, sinning more only makes things worse.
steps.whatToRemember: 'אל תרשע הרבה' does not permit a little sin. It means: if you have already sinned, do not add more.
steps.whyThisMatters: It counters the common thought 'I've already messed up, so why stop now?' The verse teaches that it is always worth stopping.

phrases.english: Rather: one who ate garlic
and his smell spreads,
should he go back and eat more garlic
so that his smell spreads even more?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse permits a little wickedness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse speaks to someone who has already sinned and warns him not to add more sin.

steps.title: The wicked are calm about their death
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב עולא reads 'חרצובות' as חרד and עצב. The wicked are neither anxious nor sad about death, and their heart is sturdy like a wide hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב עולא taught: What does the פסוק 'For there are no pangs at their death, and their body is sound' mean? הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Is it not enough that the wicked are not anxious and sad about the day of death? Their heart is also as solid for them as a hall.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It explains a פסוק in תהלים about how the wicked feel about dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חרצובות is split into two words: חרד (anxious) and עצב (sad). The wicked have neither feeling about death. On top of that, their heart is 'sturdy like an אולם.' This means it is wide open and untouched, so the thought of death never troubles them.

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ulla expounded:
What is that which is written
"For there are no pangs at their death
and their body is sound"
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Is it not enough for the wicked
that they are not anxious and sad
phrases.notes: The word חרצובות is read as חרד (anxious) plus עצב (sad) put together.

phrases.english: over the day of death,
but also their heart is sturdy for them like a hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא בַּר רַב עוּלָּא: מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from a different speaker, רבא בר רב עולא (the son of רב עולא from steps 9–10). It continues the theme of the wicked and their attitude to sin and death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wicked are untroubled by the thought of death; their hearts stay closed to it.

steps.title: רבה's verse says the same idea
steps.stepSummary: רבה's teaching matches: the wicked know their path leads to death, but fat on their kidneys (their 'כסל') blocks this awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבה said about the פסוק 'This is their way, folly for them.' The wicked know their path leads to death, but they have fat on their kidneys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar teaching from רבה to back up the previous idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כסל means both 'folly' and 'loins/kidneys.' The wicked are not ignorant, since they know where their path leads. But the fat (חלב) covering their loins, meaning dullness, stops the knowledge from reaching their heart. This supports the previous step: they know about death and still feel nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what (someone said), a matching source

phrases.english: And this is what Rabba said:
What is that which is written, "This is their way, folly for them"?
The wicked know that their path leads to death,
but they have fat on their kidneys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 11 with a parallel teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That the wicked are unmoved by death.

steps.title: Maybe they simply forget?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the wicked aren't dull at all. Maybe they just forget about death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lest you say it is just forgotten by them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible misunderstanding. This sets up the next step, which will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might excuse the wicked: they don't ignore death on purpose, they simply forget it. If that were true, the claim that they 'know' would be weakened.

phrases.english: Lest you say that it is forgotten by them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether step 12's 'knowing' might really be forgetting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is their lack of concern caused by forgetfulness?

steps.title: No, they even speak about it
steps.stepSummary: The end of the פסוק shows that they talk about their fate, so they have not forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And after them, with their mouths they speak approvingly, סלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question using the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בפיהם' means they speak about death with their own mouths. Someone who talks about a thing has not forgotten it. So their calm comes from a dulled heart, not from a gap in memory.
steps.whatToRemember: The wicked know and even speak about their end, yet their hearts stay untouched. The problem is a dulled heart, not missing knowledge.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And after them, with their mouths they speak approvingly, Selah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They speak of their fate, so it is not forgetfulness.

steps.title: Which view does רבי יוסי follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. רבי יוסי makes only the wick case liable, but neither רבי יהודה's view nor רבי שמעון's view fits that split.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Like one who spares the lamp, etc.' Whose view does רבי יוסי hold? If he holds like רבי יהודה, he should make a person liable in those other cases too! If he holds like רבי שמעון, he should exempt the wick case too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about putting out a flame on שבת. It challenges רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting out a flame to save the lamp, oil, or wick is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, meaning the act is not done for its usual purpose. רבי יהודה says you are liable for such acts, so all the cases should be liable. רבי שמעון says you are exempt, so all the cases should be exempt. רבי יוסי's split, liable only for the wick, fits neither.

keyTerms.meaning: as one who spares the lamp (quote from the משנה)
a forbidden act done not for its normal purpose

steps.confusionAlert: The phrases רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון here refer to their famous argument about מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. They are not quoted in this משנה itself.

phrases.english: "As one who spares the lamp, etc."
Rabbi Yosei: in accordance with whom does he hold?
If he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
then even in those other cases he should be liable!
And if he holds like Rabbi Shimon,
then for a wick too he should be exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's split ruling in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: each known view forces all cases to be treated the same way.

steps.title: עולא: רבי יהודה's view, plus a rule about dismantling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי follows רבי יהודה. But he holds that destroying counts as סותר only when you rebuild in the same place, and only the wick is being 'rebuilt' in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Really, he holds like רבי יהודה. But רבי יוסי holds that dismantling in order to rebuild in the same place counts as סותר. Dismantling in order to build somewhere else does not count as סותר.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge. He keeps רבי יוסי with רבי יהודה and explains the difference between the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting out a flame is a destructive act, like סותר. It counts only when it serves rebuilding in the same place. Saving the wick to relight that same wick fits this. Saving the lamp or oil is not about relighting them in the same way, so it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: in order to rebuild in the same place

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Actually, he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Yosei holds

phrases.aramaic: סוֹתֵר עַל מְנָת לִבְנוֹת בִּמְקוֹמוֹ הָוֵי סוֹתֵר.
phrases.english: that dismantling in order to rebuild in its place is considered dismantling.
In order to build not in its place —
it is not considered dismantling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a further rule that רבי יוסי holds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יהודה would make all cases liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only destroying in order to rebuild in the same place counts, and the wick case fits that.

steps.title: רבה: the משכן was rebuilt somewhere else
steps.stepSummary: All מלאכות come from the משכן, and the משכן was taken down to be rebuilt at a new place. So rebuilding elsewhere should count too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: After all, we learn all the מלאכות from the משכן. There, it was dismantling in order to build in a different place!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges עולא's rule using the source of all שבת laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model case for סותר is taking down the משכן. Each time, it was rebuilt at the next camp, which is a different place. If that is the model, then 'not in the same place' must still count, and עולא's rule falls apart.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
After all, all the labors
we derive them from the Tabernacle,
and there it was dismantling in order to build
not in its place!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: מִכְּדֵי כׇּל מְלָאכוֹת יָלְפִינַן לְהוּ מִמִּשְׁכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that סותר requires rebuilding in the same place
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case (the משכן) itself was rebuilt in a different place.

steps.title: The משכן counts as the same place
steps.stepSummary: Since the Jews camped only by ה׳'s command, taking down the משכן is treated as rebuilding in the same place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is different there. Since it is written 'By the word of ה׳ they camped,' it is like dismantling in order to rebuild in the same place.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends his rule by showing that the משכן is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every move and every camp was set by ה׳. So the next location was already decided. That makes it count as 'its place,' and עולא's rule survives.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is different there,
since it is written, "By the word of the Lord they camped,"

phrases.aramaic: כְּסוֹתֵר עַל מְנָת לִבְנוֹת בִּמְקוֹמוֹ דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: it is like dismantling in order to rebuild in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משכן was rebuilt in a different place.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because ה׳ chose every camp, it counts as the same place.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: he follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer to the original question: רבי יוסי holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Really, he holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, different answer to the question in step 15 begins. It sets up the next question about the wick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of עולא's approach, רבי יוחנן takes the other side of the dilemma. That explains why the lamp and oil cases are exempt. But it still has to explain why the wick case is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: and רבי יוחנן said (an alternative answer)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Actually, he holds like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative to עולא's answer (steps 16–18).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chooses the other side of the dilemma
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי שמעון would exempt the wick too.
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows רבי שמעון; the wick case will be explained separately.

steps.title: Then why is the wick different?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי follows רבי שמעון, why is the wick case liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is different about a wick?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses רבי יוחנן's approach on the one case it does not yet explain. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of the dilemma from step 15. Under רבי שמעון, every case should be exempt.

phrases.english: And what is different about a wick?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יוסי holds like רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון exempts מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, so the wick should be exempt too.

steps.title: A wick that needs singeing is being fixed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a new wick that needs to be singed before use. Putting it out fixes the wick, and even רבי שמעון agrees you are liable for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב המנונא said, and some say רב אדא בר אהבה: Here we are dealing with a wick that needs singeing. In that case even רבי שמעון agrees, because he is fixing a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the wick case is different, even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new wick lights better once it has been charred. Putting out the flame on purpose leaves the wick charred and ready, which is improving a utensil (מתקן מנא). That is a constructive act, not just a destructive one, so even רבי שמעון makes a person liable.

phrases.english: As Rav Hamnuna said,
and some say Rav Adda bar Ahava:
Here we are dealing with a wick that needs to be singed,
for in that case even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
because he is fixing a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wick case is an ordinary destructive act.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a wick that needs charring, so putting it out fixes a utensil.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports this
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that the משנה says 'he makes it charcoal,' which describes an intended result. This supports the singeing explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is precise too. The משנה teaches 'because he makes it into charcoal,' and it does not teach 'because it becomes charcoal.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings support for רב המנונא's answer from the exact words of the משנה. The step ends with a conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He makes it charcoal' shows the charring is the person's goal, which fits preparing a wick for use. Had it said 'it becomes charcoal,' it would sound like a side effect. 'שמע מינה' closes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise (supports this)

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: רבי יוסי follows רבי יהודה, and only סותר על מנת לבנות במקומו counts. רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי follows רבי שמעון, and the wick is liable because extinguishing it fixes the wick (מתקן מנא). The wording 'עושה פחם' supports this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even רבי שמעון, who exempts מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, makes a person liable when the act improves an object.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is also precise,
since it teaches "because he makes it into charcoal,"
and it does not teach "because it becomes charcoal."
Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 21 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the wick case involves intentional charring that prepares the wick.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה refers to deliberately charring a wick, which counts as fixing a utensil.

steps.title: Three areas where women are punished at childbirth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that women may die in childbirth for being careless in נדה, חלה, and הדלקת הנר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For three sins, women die at the time of giving birth: for not being careful with the laws of נדה, with separating חלה, and with lighting the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three מצוות that women must be careful with, and it warns of a serious punishment at childbirth for neglecting them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous discussion was about lighting שבת candles, and this משנה ends that topic with a warning. All three מצוות are ones especially connected to women. The גמרא will now explain why each one leads to danger specifically at childbirth.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of their giving birth
The portion of dough given to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source for the well-known idea that these three are special מצוות for women.

phrases.english: Mishnah: For three transgressions
women die at the time of their childbirth:
for not being careful with the laws of a menstruating woman,
with challah, and with lighting the lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת נָשִׁים מֵתוֹת בִּשְׁעַת לֵידָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה. It closes the topic of שבת lights that came before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carelessness in נדה, חלה, or הדלקת הנר can bring death at childbirth.

steps.title: Why is נדה punished at childbirth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that carelessness in נדה is punished at childbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: For נדה, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why neglecting נדה leads to danger specifically at childbirth. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a punishment but no reason for it. The גמרא wants to know the link between this sin and this particular punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A menstruating woman and the laws that apply to her

phrases.english: Gemara: Menstruation — what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why carelessness in נדה is punished specifically during childbirth.

steps.title: Measure for measure: punished in the same place she sinned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that she sinned with her womb, so she is punished through her womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: She sinned in the chambers of her womb, so she is struck in the chambers of her womb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers that the punishment matches the sin. The sin of נדה involves the womb, and so does the danger at childbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the principle of מידה כנגד מידה, measure for measure. The sin and the punishment involve the same part of the body. That explains why the punishment comes at childbirth and not at some other time.
steps.whatToRemember: נדה is explained as measure for measure: the sin and the punishment both involve the womb.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
She sinned in the chambers of her womb,
therefore she is struck in the chambers of her womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק הִיא קִלְקְלָה בְּחַדְרֵי בִטְנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about נדה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The punishment is measure for measure: she sinned with the womb, so she is punished through the womb.

steps.title: That works for נדה, but what about חלה and lighting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the 'womb' reason only explains נדה. It does not explain חלה or הדלקת הנר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for נדה. But for חלה and lighting the lamp, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether רבי יצחק's reason is enough. חלה and lighting have nothing to do with the womb, so why would they be punished at childbirth?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's measure-for-measure answer depends on a physical link to the womb. The other two מצוות in the משנה have no such link. So the גמרא needs a reason that covers them as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this case)

phrases.english: Granted, menstruation —
but challah and lighting the lamp,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח נִדָּה חַלָּה וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יצחק's answer explains only one of the three items.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The womb-based reason fits נדה but cannot explain why חלה and lighting are punished at childbirth.

steps.title: ה׳'s teaching about blood, from the Galilean scholar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching that a Galilean scholar taught before רב חסדא‎: ה׳ placed blood in people and warned about matters of blood. This explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As that Galilean scholar taught before רב חסדא: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: I placed a רביעית of blood in you, and I warned you about matters of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a Galilean scholar. ה׳ gave each person blood, and ה׳ gave a warning about blood, meaning the laws of נדה. The rest of the teaching, which covers חלה and lighting, continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is built as a pattern of 'I gave you X, and I warned you about X.' This line is only the first part of the pattern, applied to blood and נדה. The same pattern will soon be used for חלה and the lamp, which will answer the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג (a liquid measure)

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching is not finished here. The parts about חלה and lighting, which actually answer the challenge, come on the next amud.

phrases.english: As that Galilean taught
before Rav Chisda:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I placed a quarter-log of blood in you —
about matters of blood I warned you.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִדְרַשׁ הַהוּא גָּלִילָאָה עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge with a new explanation that can cover all three מצוות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the womb-based reason with a broader pattern: 'what I gave you, I warned you about.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only נדה has a reason connected to childbirth.
steps.terutzMaskana: A shared pattern of 'I gave you X and warned you about X' explains all three. It starts here with blood and נדה.
